description: Single-panel property plot headed "Fault energies in Fe-Al alloys". The y-axis is "Fault energy (mJ/m²)" from 0 to 120 with ticks every 20; the x-axis is "Aluminium content (%)" from 20 to 45 with ticks every 5. Three labelled series are shown: "APBI in B2 order" as filled circles joined by a solid straight line; "APBII in D O3 order" as squares with a hand-drawn dashed line; and "APBI in D O3 order" as open triangles with a hand-drawn dashed line (one filled circle at ~27% Al near 45 mJ/m² also falls near this series). The B2 APBI energy rises steeply and monotonically with Al content, the solid line running from about 26% Al low in the plot up to about 36% Al, where the highest point lies just below the 120 mJ/m² frame. Both D O3 series fall with increasing Al content and their dashed lines cross each other and the B2 line in the 27-29% Al region, where all three energies lie in the 60-80 mJ/m² band. No error bars and no printed data labels are present, so values are only readable approximately against gridlines. The figure demonstrates that APB energies in B2-ordered Fe-Al increase strongly with Al content, while D O3 APB energies decrease and remain only moderate (near 70-80 mJ/m²) around 25-30% Al.

subfigures.description: One scatter/line plot of fault energy (mJ/m², y-axis 0-120) versus aluminium content (%, x-axis 20-45) containing three labelled series: 'APBI in B2 order' (filled circles, solid trend line, rising with Al content), 'APBII in DO3 order' (squares, dashed line, falling with Al content) and 'APBI in DO3 order' (open triangles, dashed line, falling with Al content). All three lines cross near 27-29% Al in the 60-80 mJ/m² range.

observations.observation: The plot is titled 'Fault energies in Fe-Al alloys'.
The y-axis is labelled 'Fault energy (mJ/m²)' and spans 0 to 120 with tick marks every 20.
The x-axis is labelled 'Aluminium content (%)' and spans 20 to 45 with tick marks every 5.

Three data series are labelled inside the plot: 'APBI in B2 order' (filled circles with a solid line), 'APBII in DO3 order' (squares with a dashed line) and 'APBI in DO3 order' (open triangles with a dashed line).

The 'APBI in B2 order' series increases monotonically with Al content, from a point low in the plot (between the 20 and 40 mJ/m² gridlines, near 26% Al) up to the highest point, which sits just below the 120 mJ/m² frame at roughly 36% Al.
The two D O3 series ('APBII in DO3 order' and 'APBI in DO3 order') both decrease with increasing Al content, their dashed trend lines sloping downwards to the right.
The dashed D O3 lines cross the rising B2 APBI line in the region of about 27-29% Al, where all plotted values lie between the 60 and 80 mJ/m² gridlines.
No error bars and no printed numeric data labels appear on any data point; values are readable only approximately against the gridlines.
The caption states that the figure shows variation of APB energies in B2 ordered and DO3 ordered Fe-Al alloys as a function of Al content, with data taken from Refs. [19-21].

The citing text states that the APBI fault is trailed by a (1/2)<111> dislocation in B2-ordered material, or in material with additional DO3 order at compositions near 25-30% Al, while the APBII fault is trailed by a pair of (1/2)<111> dislocations in material with DO3 order.
The citing text states that high APB energies tend to keep partial dislocations close together, and that these values are used later to interpret observed dislocation structures.

The citing text uses Fig. 3 to argue that the relatively low APB energies for both APBI and APBII faults (with DO3 order imperfect in Fe-25% Al) explain why dislocations in Fe-25% Al remain only loosely coupled rather than forming closely coupled superdislocations.
The caption states the data derive from studies of Ray-Crawford-Cockayne (Refs. [19-21]); the image itself shows no source annotation.
